task: SOH — MAP-GEO-REJOIN-02A / Evidence Integrity Corrective & Final Map Intake
method: Corrected native 640x360 PNGs opened individually in the file viewer; every image cross-checked against its capture provenance in mapgeo02-shot-provenance.json and, where stated, against a live runtime tile-code probe. No image was graded as production visual acceptance.

inspected.subject: br_2 deck silhouette (7 AU, almost pure north)
inspected.observed: A single bounded vertical wood-plank strip crossing blue water end to end; stepped plank ends at both banks; hero stands on the deck.

inspected.subject: br_2 bank A seam
inspected.observed: Deck bottom edge meets the tan road/dirt bank with no intervening blue-water gap; hero stands on the bank at the seam.

inspected.subject: br_2 bank B seam
inspected.observed: Deck top edge meets the tan bank; no water gap; the two-bank connection is visually continuous.

inspected.subject: br_5 angled deck silhouette (7 AU)
inspected.observed: Diagonal wood band spanning the river with a staircase/jagged tile-grid edge; connects to the tan banks at top-right and bottom-left. No rails, abutments or plank-end treatment.
inspected.note: Geometry is bounded and connected; only the silhouette/edge finish is crude. Art treatment, not a physical geometry change.

inspected.subject: br_a angled bank A seam
inspected.observed: Stepped deck edge meets the diagonal bank; a small blue-water notch sits beside the first plank row. Tile-code bankSeams.connected is true, but the wood/dirt boundary reads as a raw staircase.

inspected.subject: br_1 deck at the former wood-carpet coordinate
inspected.observed: Compact diagonal plank patch (46 deck tiles) over blue water, replacing the old 656-tile land wood carpet. A short dark plank stub to the left is a PRE-EXISTING GOLD-authored legacy bridge node (bridge:br_1@1022,453, raw T.BRIDGE converted to ROAD). A 35x33 live probe found 0 cliff tiles and 0 cliff/deck overlaps here.

inspected.subject: br_7 shortest span (2 AU, 28 deck tiles)
inspected.observed: Small plank patch crossing a narrow blue channel, surrounded by tan/sand terrain. Live probe: all 28 deck tiles have candidateInfo.bridgeDeckId='br_7', sampleTile.water=true and raw tile 19 ('shallow'); 'shallow' is painted tan by the ORIGINAL painter, so the wood reads as sitting on dry ground instead of clearly spanning water.
inspected.note: Physical geometry is correct (28/28 on water). This is a visual-legibility issue inherited from the unchanged original painter, NOT a new geometry defect and NOT a permission change.

inspected.subject: br_9 UNRESOLVED crossing site
inspected.observed: Blue river with NO deck art of any kind; 0 T.BRIDGE tiles in the visible 40x23 window and candidateInfo.bridgeDeckId=null. Hero appears in water because reset(tx,ty) is a VIEWER SPAWN CONTROL, not a walkability claim.

inspected.subject: br_b UNRESOLVED crossing site (32 AU unbounded water run)
inspected.observed: Wide blue river, NO deck art; 0 T.BRIDGE tiles in the visible window. A small brown T-shaped stub at the top is the PRE-EXISTING GOLD-authored dock dk_gulfhead@1025,929 (tile code 2), not a bridge deck. Hero-in-water is a viewer spawn control, not a walkability claim.

inspected.subject: MGP-D10 corrected cliff face band at a measured face tile
inspected.observed: Thin jagged vertical grey stone band with short horizontal ledges on both sides, irregular stepped outline; NOT a filled slab; 0 production collision walls. Reads as a stylised stone wall rather than a natural rock face.
inspected.note: The 2..4/16-tile thin-band requirement is met; surface naturalness/edge treatment is the remaining art-level item.

inspected.subject: Cliff real-key QA run frame (before legs)
inspected.observed: Meadow/grass and dirt only; no cliff face band is clearly visible in-frame (only tiny grey slivers at the lower viewport edge).
inspected.note: The cliff-collision claim rests on numeric blockedSubsteps and tile-code checks (D12/E03), not on visible imagery in this run frame. A fresh-frame QA-mode capture AT the measured face tile would close the gap.

inspected.subject: Cliff real-key QA run frame (after legs)
inspected.observed: Dirt/biome transition with a few green patches; no cliff face band clearly visible in-frame.

inspected.subject: Regression check on the formerly duplicated _at_bridge family
inspected.observed: Now shows br_7's OWN small wood deck over its narrow channel, not the final canvas of an unrelated fixture. All 8 _at_bridge PNGs have distinct content hashes.

summary.deckSilhouettes: Bounded and water-only for all 10 resolved candidates; straight-axis decks (br_2) read cleanly; angled decks (br_5, br_a) have stepped tile-grid edges with no rail/abutment treatment -> targeted art rework, not a geometry defect.
summary.seams: Both measured bank approaches are visually and tile-code connected for the inspected bridges; angled seams are geometrically closed but visually crude -> targeted art rework.
summary.cliffFaces: Thin jagged band confirmed, no filled slab and no permanent wall; naturalness needs targeted art rework. The dedicated measured-face shot is good evidence; the cliff real-key run frames do NOT show the face clearly -> evidence gap.
